questions.q: State the WHO definition of reproductive health in your own words, highlighting the three dimensions of well‑being it includes.
questions.a: Correct answer: Reproductive health is a state of complete physical, mental, and social well‑being in all matters relating to the reproductive system, its functions and processes, not merely the absence of disease. It also includes the ability to have a safe, satisfying sex life and the freedom to decide if, when, and how often to reproduce. A wrong answer that omits “social well‑being” or “freedom to decide” reveals a narrow, purely biomedical understanding and misses the rights‑based perspective central to the NCERT framework.

questions.q: Explain why the WHO definition of reproductive health goes beyond the mere absence of reproductive tract infections or diseases.
questions.a: Correct answer: The definition explicitly includes positive aspects — physical, mental, and social well‑being, a satisfying and safe sex life, and reproductive autonomy. Absence of disease is necessary but not sufficient; a person may be disease‑free yet lack access to contraception, face coercion, or suffer stigma, which compromises reproductive health. A wrong answer that equates reproductive health with only disease‑free status ignores the holistic, rights‑based approach and will lead to errors in case‑based questions on reproductive health programmes.

questions.q: A 16‑year‑old girl in a rural Indian village is married early, has no access to menstrual hygiene products, and is pressured to conceive immediately. Using the four core components of reproductive health, identify which components are violated and why.
questions.a: Correct answer: (1) Physical well‑being — compromised by lack of menstrual hygiene and early pregnancy risks. (2) Mental well‑being — compromised by pressure and anxiety. (3) Social well‑being — compromised by gender norms limiting her agency. (4) Freedom to decide reproduction — violated because she cannot choose if/when to conceive. A wrong answer that lists only “early marriage is bad” without mapping to the four components shows inability to apply the definition analytically, a common error in competency‑based questions.

questions.q: Compare the scope of “general health” (Class 8 definition) and “reproductive health” (Class 12 definition). Identify two elements present in reproductive health but absent in the general health definition.
questions.a: Correct answer: General health (WHO) = physical, mental, social well‑being, not merely absence of disease. Reproductive health adds: (a) well‑being in all matters relating to the reproductive system and its functions/processes, and (b) the capability to reproduce and freedom to decide if, when, and how often. A wrong answer that says “reproductive health is just health of reproductive organs” misses the autonomy and rights dimensions, leading to incomplete answers in board exams.

questions.q: Critique the statement: “If a country eliminates all sexually transmitted infections, it has achieved reproductive health for its population.” Justify your evaluation using the WHO definition.
questions.a: Correct answer: The statement is false. Eliminating STIs addresses only the “absence of disease” part of physical well‑being. Reproductive health also requires mental and social well‑being, safe/satisfying sex life, and reproductive autonomy. A population could be STI‑free but still face forced sterilisation, child marriage, or lack of contraceptive choice — violating reproductive health. A wrong answer that agrees reveals confusion between disease control and comprehensive reproductive health, a trap in assertion‑reason questions.

questions.q: Design a one‑page poster for a school health programme that communicates the four pillars of reproductive health to adolescents. Sketch the layout and write the key message for each pillar in simple Hindi/English.
questions.a: Expected answer: Poster with four quadrants: (1) “शरीर की देखभाल” (Physical) — hygiene, nutrition, regular check‑ups. (2) “मन की शांति” (Mental) — stress management, saying no to pressure. (3) “समाज में सम्मान” (Social) — gender equality, no stigma. (4) “अपना फैसला” (Autonomy) — right to choose marriage, contraception, family size. A poor answer that only shows pictures of condoms or says “avoid AIDS” indicates a narrow, protection‑only mindset and failure to internalise the holistic definition.
